name: Prompt adherence v1
description: Twenty text-to-image cases scored with CLIPScore against the short form of their prompt: does the picture show what was asked for. Weak by construction and useful anyway — it is what catches a quantization that has stopped following the prompt rather than merely become softer.

eval.notes: CLIPScore is 100 * max(cosine(image, text), 0) against the row's answer, which is the short form of the prompt because CLIP truncates at 77 tokens. An item counts as correct above params.clipscore_min; the per-item score in items[].metrics is the number worth reading. Two lanes within a point of each other are not distinguishable by this metric and should not be ranked by it.

notes: The render shape comes from each row's meta.render, not from params: these are frozen cases, and a case rendered at another size or seed is a different picture. params carries only what is the same for all of them. The CLIP model is part of the measurement: ViT-L-14/openai is the pinned default and a score from another backbone is a different scale. ImageReward is deliberately not the default — its pins (timm 0.6.13, fairscale sdist-only) conflict with open_clip in one environment, so it belongs in a separate run if it is used at all.
